application.target: Portcode QA Calibration native WebView2 app
application.automationProcedure: Drive the running native WebView2 through its loopback CDP endpoint, never through a separate web-preview browser. Use `node .qa/scripts/webview-cdp.mjs info`, `node .qa/scripts/webview-cdp.mjs eval --file <repository-relative-script.js>`, and `node .qa/scripts/webview-cdp.mjs screenshot --output <repository-relative-image.png>`. Put evaluation scripts and screenshots only beneath the current run artifact root. The calibration frontend exposes only the constrained `window.__PORTCODE_QA__` API: resetScenario, seedLocalComposer, validation defer/reject/resolve, agent defer/accept/reject/emit, session select/disappear, remote enter/emit/leave, and snapshot. Use those controls only to make app-owned asynchronous states deterministic; never mutate raw Zustand state, invoke arbitrary native commands, or use real account data. To exercise real Rust validation, create synthetic fixtures beneath the current run artifact root, arm validation.deferNext({ useNativeResult: true }), dispatch the existing DOM drop procedure, inspect the pending UI, then release the returned operation id. runAgent is fail-closed in this build: click Send only after agent.deferNext(), then explicitly accept/reject and emit synthetic StreamEvent values. An unarmed provider path must remain denied.
application.resetProcedure: This binary uses the isolated dev.porthex.portcode.qa-calibration app config/database and qa-calibration WebView profile, never the user's normal Portcode profile. Call window.__PORTCODE_QA__.resetScenario() before each independent controlled scenario; it invalidates stale deferred callbacks and clears QA fixture state. Then seed only the required local or remote scenario. Use only synthetic fixtures beneath the run artifact root. Never copy or alter real accounts/settings.
limitations: No live provider call is allowed, so provider-side interpretation is established from protocol fidelity and deterministic tests rather than a paid end-to-end turn.

The operating-system file-picker chrome is platform-owned and not applicable to app screenshot coverage. Portcode-owned Attach states, picker options/normalization, cancellation/focus restoration, and returned-path behavior remain required.
The QA binary must be prebuilt from .qa/tauri.qa.conf.json before invoking the runner.
